test_meta.title: ST – Practice Set B: Surgical Instrumentation & Mayo Stand Setup

questions.stem: Which knife handle is long and slender, designed to hold small blades (#10, #11, #12, #15) in deep, narrow surgical cavities (such as tonsillectomy or pelvic surgery)?
questions.explanation: #7 knife handle is long, thin, and contoured to hold blades (#10, #11, #12, #15) in deep, confined cavities.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 344

questions.stem: Which scalpel handle is larger and heavier, designed to hold larger blades like #20, #21, and #22 for thick tissue incisions in autopsies or heavy trauma?
questions.explanation: #4 scalpel handle is wider and accommodates the larger #20-series blades (#20 through #25).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 345

questions.stem: Which delicate dissecting scissors feature fine, sharp-tipped blades used extensively in ophthalmic, plastic, and reconstructive microsurgery?
questions.explanation: Iris scissors have very small, razor-sharp blades originally created for ophthalmic iridectomy, now ubiquitous in plastic and fine soft tissue surgery.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 349

questions.stem: What specialized angled scissors have a blunt probe nodule on the lower blade to slip safely beneath dressings, casts, or umbilical cords without piercing patient skin?
questions.explanation: Lister bandage scissors feature an angled blade with a rounded, blunt probe tip on the lower blade designed to slide against patient skin without cutting it.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 350

questions.stem: Which vascular scissors are angled at 45 or 60 degrees, designed specifically for extending an arteriotomy in coronary or peripheral vascular vessels?
questions.explanation: Potts-Smith scissors have angled fine blades tailored to extend incisions into arteries and veins smoothly without tearing the opposite vessel wall.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 21, pg 626

questions.stem: Which hemostatic clamp has transverse serrations extending only halfway down the length of its jaws?
questions.explanation: Kelly clamps feature serrations along only the distal half of the jaws, whereas Crile clamps have serrations along the full length of the jaws.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 351

questions.stem: Which heavy hemostatic forceps has full transverse serrations and broad jaws, used for clamping large vascular pedicles and tough fibrous tissue bundles?
questions.explanation: Rochester-Pean clamps are heavy, robust forceps with transverse serrations along the full jaw length designed to occlude larger blood vessels and tissue pedicles.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 352

questions.stem: Which tissue forceps has a small, delicate triangular fenestration with fine 1x2 teeth at the tip, commonly used by plastic and general surgeons for grasping skin edges during suturing?
questions.explanation: Adson tissue forceps feature a broad thumb grasp tapering to fine tips with 1x2 interlocking teeth, ideal for handling skin margins during subcuticular closure.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 355

questions.stem: Which heavy tissue forceps features large rounded, cup-shaped spoon tips with radiating circular teeth, frequently used for grasping dense tissues or retrieving gallstones?
questions.explanation: Russian tissue forceps have broad, circular, spoon-shaped tips with radiating grooves, providing a secure grip on slippery pelvic tissues, liver, or gallstones.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 357

questions.stem: Which perforated towel clamp has sharp, curved interlocking points used to anchor surgical drapes or hold reduction on small bone fragments?
questions.explanation: The Backhaus towel clamp has sharp piercing points designed to penetrate drapes and secure towels. Once clamped through drapes, the tips are contaminated.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 359

questions.stem: If a sharp Backhaus towel clamp is removed from a draped patient during surgery, what is the sterility status of the clamp tips?
options: The tips are considered contaminated and the clamp must be passed off the field without touching the sterile table
The tips remain sterile if Betadine was applied to the drape
The clamp can be reused anywhere on the Mayo stand
The clamp can be wiped with a wet Ray-Tec and reused
questions.explanation: Because the sharp tips penetrated through sterile drapes into unsterile patient skin, the tips are contaminated and must be immediately removed from the sterile field.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 7, pg 185

questions.stem: Which handheld retractor features a solid right-angle blade with a concave lip on a sturdy handle, widely used in pairs for deep abdominal wall and laparotomy exposure?
questions.explanation: The Richardson retractor is a standard right-angle abdominal wall retractor with a contoured handle and curved lip, designed for heavy fascial and muscular retraction.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 361

questions.stem: Which double-ended hand-held retractor has a narrow right-angle blade on one end and a three-pronged rake (sharp or blunt) on the other, commonly used in plastic and hand surgery?
questions.explanation: The Senn retractor is a small handheld instrument with a solid right-angle blade on one end and a 3-pronged rake on the opposite end, used in superficial soft tissue work.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 362

questions.stem: Which deep visceral retractor features a heart-shaped, flexible blade with a padded tip designed to retract the liver during upper GI and biliary surgery without bruising parenchyma?
questions.explanation: The Harrington retractor features a wide, heart-shaped blade with a rounded smooth tip specifically designed to retract the liver gently during open laparotomy.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 502

questions.stem: Which bone cutting instrument has sharp scoop-shaped, cup-like jaws designed to bite away and gouge out small pieces of cortical bone or tissue?
questions.explanation: A rongeur (single- or double-action) has sharp cupped jaws used to bite away bone fragments, cartilage, or spur tissue in orthopedic and spinal surgeries.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 606

questions.stem: Which chisel-like instrument is beveled on both sides and used with a surgical mallet to cut or shape bone during orthopedic reconstructions?
options: Bone chisel (beveled on one side only)
questions.explanation: An osteotome is beveled on both cutting sides (sloping from both faces to the edge) for dividing bone; a chisel is beveled on one side only.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 607

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to scrape away diseased bone, cartilage, or uterine endometrial lining during diagnostic and therapeutic procedures?
questions.explanation: A curette has a cup, ring, or oval scoop with sharp or blunt edges used to debride, scrape, and sample biological tissue from cavities or bone surfaces.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 18, pg 548

questions.stem: Which instrument with a sharp, slightly curved flat edge is used by the CST to strip periosteum cleanly off bone shafts before plating?
options: Periosteal elevator (e.g., Cobb, Key, or Freer)
questions.explanation: Periosteal elevators (such as the Key, Cobb, or Freer) feature flat, slightly curved blades designed to peel and elevate periosteal tissue off cortical bone surfaces.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 605

questions.stem: Which flexible wire saw with detachable T-shaped handles is used for manual transection of bone, such as in amputations or cranial flap elevation?
questions.explanation: The Gigli saw is a flexible twisted wire with sharp teeth pulled back and forth across bone between two manual handles to perform controlled osteotomies.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 609

questions.stem: Which forceps has long, thin ring-handled shanks terminating in smooth, ring-shaped fenestrations used to hold Ray-Tec sponges for prep sticks or deep cavity swabbing?
questions.explanation: The Foerster sponge-holding forceps (ring forceps) has smooth or serrated circular loop jaws designed to hold folded gauze sponges for abdominal prepping or deep blotting.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 356

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a laparoscopic Veress needle?
options: Blind percutaneous entry through the fascia into the peritoneal cavity to instill CO2 gas and establish initial pneumoperitoneum safely
questions.explanation: The Veress needle features a sharp outer cannula with an internal spring-loaded blunt stylet designed to safely puncture the abdominal wall for blind CO2 insufflation.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 13, pg 434

questions.stem: Which alternative laparoscopic entry technique uses a blunt-tipped cannula (Hasson trocar) placed under direct surgical cutdown visualization to eliminate blind trocar visceral injury?
questions.explanation: The Hasson open technique involves making a small periumbilical incision, incising fascia under direct vision, placing stay sutures, and inserting a blunt Hasson trocar.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 13, pg 436

questions.stem: What is the recommended maximum intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) setting on the CO2 insufflator during adult laparoscopic surgery to prevent vena cava compression and respiratory compromise?
questions.explanation: Standard adult laparoscopic pneumoperitoneum is maintained between 12 and 15 mmHg. Pressures above 15 mmHg impede venous return to the heart and reduce cardiac output.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 13, pg 438

questions.stem: What solution should be kept on the sterile Mayo stand to clean tissue coagulum and blood from the tips of electrosurgical pencils and bipolar forceps?
options: Sterile water and a scratch pad (ESU tip cleaner)
questions.explanation: Sterile water is preferred over saline for cleaning electrocautery tips and wiping instruments because saline contains sodium chloride, which corrodes and pits stainless steel.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 368

questions.stem: How should delicate microsurgical and eye instruments be cleaned and handled during surgery?
options: Wiped gently with a lint-free non-fibrous microsponge (e.g., Weck-cel) and kept in a designated silicone protective rack
Allowed to dry with blood on hinges
questions.explanation: Microsurgical instruments have fragile tips that bend easily. They must be cleaned with lint-free microsponges (Weck-Cel) and protected in tip-guards or silicone-cushioned trays.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 11, pg 372

questions.stem: Which uterine dilator set consists of double-ended graduated cylindrical metal rods with slightly curved rounded tips, numbered in half-millimeter increments for cervical dilation?
questions.explanation: Hegar dilators are curved, double-ended, smooth cylindrical dilators used sequentially to dilate the cervical os prior to curettage or hysteroscopy.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 18, pg 549

questions.stem: Which set of graduated malleable metal probes with oval olive-shaped tips is used by the surgeon to explore and calibrate the common bile duct during open CBD exploration?
questions.explanation: Bakes dilators have flexible shafts with graduated olive-shaped tips used to explore, dilate, and calibrate the common bile duct and sphincter of Oddi.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 506

questions.stem: Which self-retaining retractor is specifically designed for mastoidectomy, laminectomy, and anterior cervical discectomy with interchangeable blunt and sharp blades on a pivoting frame?
questions.explanation: The Beckman (or Cloward) retractor features hinged arms with interchangeable blades that articulate to conform to spinal or mastoid operative margins.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 23, pg 690

questions.stem: What mechanical counting device on the Mayo stand is essential for securely organizing and safely counting detached surgical needles during a procedure?
options: Magnetic or foam needle counter box
questions.explanation: Used needles must be parked immediately into numbered foam or magnetic needle count boxes to keep sharps immobilized, visible, and safely countable.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 10, pg 314

questions.stem: Which vascular bulldog clamp is small, spring-loaded, cross-action, and used directly on smaller peripheral blood vessels to temporarily halt blood flow during microvascular repair?
questions.explanation: Bulldog clamps are miniature, spring-loaded vascular clamps with atraumatic teeth that pinch small vessels temporarily without crushing the lumen.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 21, pg 627
